pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

7	+# Match information (intel)
8	+
9	+The pure rules behind §2's timed reveals, §3's rumors and journal, §5's final-island announcement and §11's comeback leads. `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel` has the config, the state, `stepIntel`, `targetedRumorAvailability`, `replayIntel` and the three lead phases (`gatherLeads`, `decideLeads`, `answerRequests`). `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel` has the constants and the zod validator `validateIntelRules`. The module doesn't import the ledger. It is integer data with no clocks and no `Math.random`, and time is the world tick (20 per second). `objectives-endgame` wires it into `MatchRoom`; nothing calls it yet.
10	+
11	+## Constants (`intelRules`)
12	+
13	+| Rule | Value |
14	+| --- | --- |
15	+| Sector grid | 3 × 3, named row by row from "North-West Reach" to "South-East Reach" |
16	+| Sighting delay | 600 ticks (30 s), equal to the carrier interval |
17	+| Carrier interval | 600 ticks (30 s) |
18	+| Sector reveal | 24,000 ticks (minute 20) after control start |
19	+| Carrier reveal | 33,600 ticks (minute 28) after control start |
20	+| Targeted rumor price | 25 gold (the caller charges it) |
21	+
22	+The validator refuses a zero interval, reveals out of order, a carrier reveal that isn't a multiple of the interval, a delay that differs from the interval, and names that are missing or repeated. Because the carrier reveal is a multiple of the interval, every broadcast falls on a snapshot boundary, so pending and new sightings can't split across messages.
23	+
24	+## Sectors
25	+
26	+`sectorOfTile` cuts the map's columns and rows into three bands each by integer division (`floor(tile × 3 / width)`). Every tile is in exactly one sector, and bands differ by at most one tile. On the 224 × 208 slice sea, the columns start at tiles 0, 75 and 150 and the rows at 0, 70 and 139. `sectorOf(position)` is the sector of the position's tile. A position off the map counts in the nearest edge sector. The config computes all of this from the map size, so the same code serves the slice and the 12-island alpha.
27	+
28	+## Leads
29	+
30	+A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island**, where a source of that type is still sealed, or a **sector**, where a recovery cache holds one. It never names a rubbing, a player or a position. It picks among the eligible targets, sorted, with the seeded generator (`random.ts`) keyed by (seed, tick, player, type), so the same seed gives the same rumor and no other decision changes it. It tries three tiers in order:
31	+
32	+1. the islands with a sealed source of the type;
33	+2. the sectors with a cached copy;
34	+3. a **carrier sighting**, and only when every copy of the type is carried by someone else.
35	+
36	+Targets already active in the player's journal are skipped, so a player is never given the same lead twice.
37	+
38	+Leads are made on four occasions:
39	+
40	+- a **start** rumor for each player at control start, or when a player is first seen after it. It only ever names a source or a cache, of any type the player lacks. When every copy of every missing type is carried (a late joiner, say), there is no starting rumor, only a `no-lead`: a start never becomes a carrier sighting;
41	+- a free **fresh** rumor for each type a player lost (§11);
42	+- a **targeted** rumor, bought on request;
43	+- a **replacement**, when a journal rumor goes stale.
44	+
45	+Losses and completions come from diffing each player's held types between ticks. A rubbing reserved in a duel still counts as held, so entering a duel is never a loss; only a settled theft is.
46	+
47	+**Journal rumors** (island or sector) are the only leads tracked:
48	+
49	+- A rumor goes **stale** when its target no longer holds its type: the source was collected or the cache claimed by someone else. The player gets `rumor-stale` with the tick and then a replacement.
50	+- A rumor whose type the holder obtains, by any means, is **resolved** quietly. It gets no replacement.
51	+
52	+**Carrier sightings** are one-shot messages, never tracked, so they can never go stale and can't be used to follow a carrier. At every carrier boundary (control start plus a multiple of 30 s, counted when crossed), the state takes one snapshot of the carried copies: the sector, the type and the internal holder of each. It keeps the latest two. A sighting reads the **older** of the two, so it is 30–60 s old and never the current position. It also skips the requester's own former entries.
53	+
54	+Only three triggers ask for a sighting: a loss (`fresh`), a journal replacement and a targeted request. The sighting's reason type (`CarrierSightingReason`) has only these three, so a start can't produce one. A `carrier-sighting` message may list several types: one entry per type (the type, the trigger's reason and a sector), all from the same older snapshot. Before minute 28, a player gets at most **one sighting message per snapshot**, and at any time at most **one per step**.
55	+
56	+**Three phases per step.** Every step builds its lead decisions the same way, whatever order the triggers, the requests or the view's arrays come in:
57	+
58	+1. **Gather.** Every trigger joins a set keyed by **(player, type)**: a type lost, a stale rumor's replacement, a pending type at a boundary (the pending set is decided again there), a targeted request. An entry keeps one free trigger (the earliest, then `fresh` before `replacement`) and its request ids, sorted.
59	+2. **Decide.** Per player by id: a starting rumor first (a source or a cache, never a sighting), then each entry in type order. An entry gets a journal rumor, a `no-lead` (free triggers only), or its type joins the player's one sighting decision. Uncapped (no sighting yet in this snapshot, or minute 28 on), one message lists every such type the older snapshot shows another player carrying; capped, nothing is sent and the free types join the one pending set (a paid type is never queued). A free type the snapshot can't answer yet also waits. Each draw uses a generator keyed by (seed, tick, player, type), and a sighting's sector by (seed, snapshot tick, player, type) among the sorted candidate sectors, so no decision depends on another.
60	+3. **Answer.** Each (player, type)'s requests, by request id (`answerRequests`):
61	+   - `covered` (not charged) when a free trigger or the start already gave the player that type in this step, as a rumor or in the sighting message;
62	+   - otherwise `rumor` or `sighting` for the first request, and `covered` for the rest;
63	+   - when nothing is delivered for that (player, type), every request gets the same `capped` or `none`.
64	+
65	+A type goes out with its free trigger's reason if it has one, otherwise `targeted`. So a player who loses two types on one tick, or at a boundary with a type already pending, or loses one while buying another, learns about all of them in one message, and a purchase is never charged for what the step gives for free. Skipped ticks change nothing: two losses seen in one batched view make one message. Two players' requests never affect each other.
66	+
67	+**Targeted requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`, and each gets exactly one outcome, whatever the order of the batch:
68	+
69	+- `rumor` or `sighting`: something was delivered. Charge the 25 gold only for these two.
70	+- `covered`: this step already gives the player that type, for free or to a request of the same type lower by id. Not charged.
71	+- `capped`: the player already got a sighting in this snapshot (before this step).
72	+- `none`: nothing to sell. The player holds the type, or the player is unknown, or it is before control start, or no untracked target exists.
73	+- `duplicate`: the request id was seen before, or is listed twice in one batch (only its lowest (player, type) is taken). The step answers it without changing the state or drawing from the generator.
74	+
75	+`targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, view, playerId, type)` gives the same answer without drawing, so the UI can show whether buying would yield anything. A later step can differ only if it crosses a snapshot boundary first, or answer `covered` when a free trigger of that player and type in the same step gives the type anyway.
76	+
77	+## Reveals (§2, §5)
78	+
79	+All reveals fire when their tick is crossed since the last processed tick, so a skipped tick never loses one. Nothing is sent before control start.
80	+
81	+- **First full set:** the first player to hold every type of the preset triggers `final-sector` (the final island's sector) to everyone. Each holder of a full set gets `final-route` with the exact point: the first completer, later completers, and anyone who restores a broken set (with `restored: true`). A player who loses a type gets `final-route-inactive`.
82	+- **Minute 20:** `sector-reveal` to everyone, listing the sectors with sealed sources and the sectors with caches.
83	+- **Minute 28, then every 30 s:** `carrier-report` to everyone, listing the (sector, type) pairs of the newest snapshot. Skipping several beats sends one report.
84	+- **Minute 35** belongs to the claim code.
85	+
86	+## Messages and hidden information (§16)
87	+
88	+`stepIntel(config, state, view, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }` never writes into its input. Each message is `{ to, body }`, where `to` is `{ kind: "player", playerId }`, `{ kind: "players", playerIds }` or `{ kind: "everyone" }`. Broadcasts are `final-sector`, `sector-reveal` and `carrier-report`; every other kind goes to one player.
89	+
90	+Bodies carry sectors, island indexes and names, types, ticks and journal entry numbers. They never carry a player id, a rubbing id, or a source's, cache's or ship's position. The one exact position ever sent is the final island's, in a `final-route` to a full-set holder. The property tests check every message of every run against these rules:
91	+
92	+- six seeded runs with compressed reveal times;
93	+- one slice run with the real constants for 36,660 ticks;
94	+- one alpha run with the real constants that skips ticks.
95	+
96	+The same runs also check, after every step, that each player got at most one sighting message in it, that every free trigger needing a sighting (a loss, or a stale rumor's replacement) is either in that step's message or in the pending set, and that it waits only if the player's sighting was already spent in this snapshot or the older snapshot shows no other carrier of it. They also check that each player has at most one pending sighting message and that every deferred type goes out at the first boundary after it was capped (or is dropped only when the checker finds it ineligible, or kept only when the previous snapshot shows no other carrier of it). Every rumor is checked against the preference: a cache lead only when no sealed source of the type is left outside the player's journal, a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists. Every sighting's reason is checked to be `fresh`, `targeted` or `replacement`. Per step and (player, type), at most one request is charged, only for a lead of that type sent with the reason `targeted`, and a `covered` request always has a lead of its type in that step. A black-box check replays the compressed runs, with extra purchases added, against the same script with each step's requests and view arrays shuffled, and compares the messages, the outcomes sorted by request id and `hashState`. Their `EXERCISED` check asserts that every message kind, outcome and lead path occurred, including a deferred delivery, a free trigger sighted in its own step and a message with several types.
97	+
98	+## Building the world view from the ledger
99	+
100	+On each processed tick, the caller passes `{ tick, players, rubbings }`:
101	+
102	+- **`players`:** each player still in the match (`status` not `left`), with the ship's position in sub-units.
103	+- **`rubbings`:** each ledger rubbing with its `type` and its `location` resolved to a place:
104	+  - `source` becomes `{ kind: "source", island, x, y }` from its `LedgerSource`;
105	+  - `cache` becomes `{ kind: "cache", x, y }` from its `LedgerCache`;
106	+  - `player` becomes `{ kind: "carried", playerId }`;
107	+  - `duel` becomes `{ kind: "duel", playerId }`.
108	+
109	+Held types and claimed-out islands (islands with no sealed source left) follow from the rubbings, so they can't disagree with them. The ledger's sticky `freshRumors` flag isn't read. The config comes from `createIntelConfig({ preset, finalIsland, controlStartTick, map })`. The state comes from `createIntelState(config, seed)`, which starts before control start.
110	+
111	+## Decisions taken here
112	+
113	+- Held types and claimed-out islands are derived from the view's rubbings rather than passed separately.
114	+- A pending sighting is one message per player holding a set of types, so two types that need a sighting at once are delivered together at the next boundary, not one interval apart, and the cap stays one sighting message per 30 s before minute 28.
115	+- Every trigger of a step joins the step's set of (player, type) entries, with one sighting decision per player, so "learns about both at once" holds on every path: several losses, a loss with a replacement or a purchase, a batched view, and the boundary tick.
116	+- A start points only at sources and caches. Sightings come only from a loss, a targeted rumor or a journal replacement.
117	+- A free trigger that finds every copy carried but no snapshot entry to read yet waits like a capped one.
118	+- A targeted request whose type a free trigger (or the start) of the same step gives the player is `covered` and not charged; the type goes out with the free reason. Of two requests for one (player, type) in one step, the first by id is charged and the other `covered`. Before, both were charged.
119	+- Leads are decided in three phases (gather by (player, type), decide with keyed draws, answer grouped by (player, type)), so order independence holds by construction, and one player's purchase never changes another's result or draw.
120	+- The state's `rng` is the seed of the keyed draws and no longer advances.

224	+import { z } from "zod";
225	+import { formatIssues, type ValidationResult } from "../rules.js";
226	+import { WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND } from "../sailing.js";
227	+
228	+/** The sea is split into a grid of named sectors this many columns wide and rows high (§2's "sectors"). */
229	+export const SECTOR_COLUMNS = 3;
230	+export const SECTOR_ROWS = 3;
231	+
232	+/** The nine sector names, row by row from the north-west corner. */
233	+export const SECTOR_NAMES = [
234	+  "North-West Reach",
235	+  "Northern Waters",
236	+  "North-East Reach",
237	+  "Western Waters",
238	+  "Central Waters",
239	+  "Eastern Waters",
240	+  "South-West Reach",
241	+  "Southern Waters",
242	+  "South-East Reach",
243	+] as const;
244	+
245	+/**
246	+ * §11: a carrier sighting is coarse and delayed. It reads the carrier snapshot taken one interval before the latest,
247	+ * so it is at least this old (and less than twice this old), never the current location.
248	+ */
249	+export const CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS = 30;
250	+/** §2: from minute 28 the carriers' sectors are published every 30 seconds; the carrier snapshots keep the same beat. */
251	+export const CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30;
252	+/** §2: at minute 20 the sectors holding unclaimed rubbings and abandoned caches are revealed. */
253	+export const SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE = 20;
254	+/** §2: from minute 28 the carriers' approximate sectors are published. */
255	+export const CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE = 28;
256	+/** §11: what the caller charges for a targeted rumor that delivers something. */
257	+export const TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD = 25;
258	+
259	+/** The information rules (§2, §3, §11) in world ticks (20 a second), counted from the start of player control. */
260	+export const intelRulesSchema = z
261	+  .strictObject({
262	+    sectorColumns: z.int().positive(),
263	+    sectorRows: z.int().positive(),
264	+    /** Row by row from the north-west; one unique, non-empty name per sector. */
265	+    sectorNames: z.array(z.string().min(1)),
266	+    /** How old a carrier sighting is at least; it must equal the carrier interval, since sightings read the previous snapshot. */
267	+    sightingDelayTicks: z.int().positive(),
268	+    /** The beat of the carrier snapshots, of the sighting cap and, from the carrier reveal on, of the carrier broadcasts. */
269	+    carrierIntervalTicks: z.int().positive(),
270	+    /** Ticks from control start to the reveal of the sectors holding unclaimed rubbings and caches. */
271	+    sectorRevealTicks: z.int().positive(),
272	+    /** Ticks from control start to the first carrier broadcast: a multiple of the carrier interval, so it falls on a snapshot boundary. */
273	+    carrierRevealTicks: z.int().positive(),
274	+    targetedRumorGold: z.int().nonnegative(),
275	+  })
276	+  .superRefine((rules, ctx) => {
277	+    if (rules.sectorNames.length !== rules.sectorColumns * rules.sectorRows) {
278	+      ctx.addIssue({
279	+        code: "custom",
280	+        path: ["sectorNames"],
281	+        message: `${rules.sectorNames.length} names for a ${rules.sectorColumns} × ${rules.sectorRows} grid`,
282	+      });
283	+    }
284	+    if (new Set(rules.sectorNames).size !== rules.sectorNames.length) {
285	+      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["sectorNames"], message: "sector names must be unique" });
286	+    }
287	+    if (rules.sightingDelayTicks !== rules.carrierIntervalTicks) {
288	+      ctx.addIssue({
289	+        code: "custom",
290	+        path: ["sightingDelayTicks"],
291	+        message: `the sighting delay (${rules.sightingDelayTicks} ticks) must equal the carrier interval (${rules.carrierIntervalTicks} ticks)`,
292	+      });
293	+    }
294	+    if (rules.sectorRevealTicks >= rules.carrierRevealTicks) {
295	+      ctx.addIssue({
296	+        code: "custom",
297	+        path: ["carrierRevealTicks"],
298	+        message: `the carrier reveal (${rules.carrierRevealTicks} ticks) must come after the sector reveal (${rules.sectorRevealTicks} ticks)`,
299	+      });
300	+    }
301	+    // The broadcasts must fall on snapshot boundaries, so a pending sighting and a new one never split across messages.
302	+    if (rules.carrierIntervalTicks > 0 && rules.carrierRevealTicks % rules.carrierIntervalTicks !== 0) {
303	+      ctx.addIssue({
304	+        code: "custom",
305	+        path: ["carrierRevealTicks"],
306	+        message: `the carrier reveal (${rules.carrierRevealTicks} ticks) must be a multiple of the carrier interval (${rules.carrierIntervalTicks} ticks)`,
307	+      });
308	+    }
309	+  });
310	+
311	+export type IntelRules = z.infer<typeof intelRulesSchema>;
312	+
313	+export const intelRules: IntelRules = {
314	+  sectorColumns: SECTOR_COLUMNS,
315	+  sectorRows: SECTOR_ROWS,
316	+  sectorNames: [...SECTOR_NAMES],
317	+  sightingDelayTicks: CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
318	+  carrierIntervalTicks: CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
319	+  sectorRevealTicks: SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE * 60 * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
320	+  carrierRevealTicks: CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE * 60 * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
321	+  targetedRumorGold: TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD,
322	+};
323	+
324	+export function validateIntelRules(candidate: unknown): ValidationResult<IntelRules> {
325	+  const parsed = intelRulesSchema.safeParse(candidate);
326	+  return parsed.success ? { ok: true, value: parsed.data } : { ok: false, issues: formatIssues(parsed.error) };
327	+}

@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+# Match information (intel)
+
+The pure rules behind §2's timed reveals, §3's rumors and journal, §5's final-island announcement and §11's comeback leads. `@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel` has the config, the state, `stepIntel`, `targetedRumorAvailability`, `replayIntel` and the three lead phases (`gatherLeads`, `decideLeads`, `answerRequests`). `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel` has the constants and the zod validator `validateIntelRules`. The module doesn't import the ledger. It is integer data with no clocks and no `Math.random`, and time is the world tick (20 per second). `objectives-endgame` wires it into `MatchRoom`; nothing calls it yet.
+
+## Constants (`intelRules`)
+
+| Rule | Value |
+| --- | --- |
+| Sector grid | 3 × 3, named row by row from "North-West Reach" to "South-East Reach" |
+| Sighting delay | 600 ticks (30 s), equal to the carrier interval |
+| Carrier interval | 600 ticks (30 s) |
+| Sector reveal | 24,000 ticks (minute 20) after control start |
+| Carrier reveal | 33,600 ticks (minute 28) after control start |
+| Targeted rumor price | 25 gold (the caller charges it) |
+
+The validator refuses a zero interval, reveals out of order, a carrier reveal that isn't a multiple of the interval, a delay that differs from the interval, and names that are missing or repeated. Because the carrier reveal is a multiple of the interval, every broadcast falls on a snapshot boundary, so pending and new sightings can't split across messages.
+
+## Sectors
+
+`sectorOfTile` cuts the map's columns and rows into three bands each by integer division (`floor(tile × 3 / width)`). Every tile is in exactly one sector, and bands differ by at most one tile. On the 224 × 208 slice sea, the columns start at tiles 0, 75 and 150 and the rows at 0, 70 and 139. `sectorOf(position)` is the sector of the position's tile. A position off the map counts in the nearest edge sector. The config computes all of this from the map size, so the same code serves the slice and the 12-island alpha.
+
+## Leads
+
+A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island**, where a source of that type is still sealed, or a **sector**, where a recovery cache holds one. It never names a rubbing, a player or a position. It picks among the eligible targets, sorted, with the seeded generator (`random.ts`) keyed by (seed, tick, player, type), so the same seed gives the same rumor and no other decision changes it. It tries three tiers in order:
+
+1. the islands with a sealed source of the type;
+2. the sectors with a cached copy;
+3. a **carrier sighting**, and only when every copy of the type is carried by someone else.
+
+Targets already active in the player's journal are skipped, so a player is never given the same lead twice.
+
+Leads are made on four occasions:
+
+- a **start** rumor for each player at control start, or when a player is first seen after it. It only ever names a source or a cache, of any type the player lacks. When every copy of every missing type is carried (a late joiner, say), there is no starting rumor, only a `no-lead`: a start never becomes a carrier sighting;
+- a free **fresh** rumor for each type a player lost (§11);
+- a **targeted** rumor, bought on request;
+- a **replacement**, when a journal rumor goes stale.
+
+Losses and completions come from diffing each player's held types between ticks. A rubbing reserved in a duel still counts as held, so entering a duel is never a loss; only a settled theft is.
+
+**Journal rumors** (island or sector) are the only leads tracked:
+
+- A rumor goes **stale** when its target no longer holds its type: the source was collected or the cache claimed by someone else. The player gets `rumor-stale` with the tick and then a replacement.
+- A rumor whose type the holder obtains, by any means, is **resolved** quietly. It gets no replacement.
+
+**Carrier sightings** are one-shot messages, never tracked, so they can never go stale and can't be used to follow a carrier. At every carrier boundary (control start plus a multiple of 30 s, counted when crossed), the state takes one snapshot of the carried copies: the sector, the type and the internal holder of each. It keeps the latest two. A sighting reads the **older** of the two, so it is 30–60 s old and never the current position. It also skips the requester's own former entries.
+
+Only three triggers ask for a sighting: a loss (`fresh`), a journal replacement and a targeted request. The sighting's reason type (`CarrierSightingReason`) has only these three, so a start can't produce one. A `carrier-sighting` message may list several types: one entry per type (the type, the trigger's reason and a sector), all from the same older snapshot. Before minute 28, a player gets at most **one sighting message per snapshot**, and at any time at most **one per step**.
+
+**Three phases per step.** Every step builds its lead decisions the same way, whatever order the triggers, the requests or the view's arrays come in:
+
+1. **Gather.** Every trigger joins a set keyed by **(player, type)**: a type lost, a stale rumor's replacement, a pending type at a boundary (the pending set is decided again there), a targeted request. An entry keeps one free trigger (the earliest, then `fresh` before `replacement`) and its request ids, sorted.
+2. **Decide.** Per player by id: a starting rumor first (a source or a cache, never a sighting), then each entry in type order. An entry gets a journal rumor, a `no-lead` (free triggers only), or its type joins the player's one sighting decision. Uncapped (no sighting yet in this snapshot, or minute 28 on), one message lists every such type the older snapshot shows another player carrying; capped, nothing is sent and the free types join the one pending set (a paid type is never queued). A free type the snapshot can't answer yet also waits. Each draw uses a generator keyed by (seed, tick, player, type), and a sighting's sector by (seed, snapshot tick, player, type) among the sorted candidate sectors, so no decision depends on another.
+3. **Answer.** Each (player, type)'s requests, by request id (`answerRequests`):
+   - `covered` (not charged) when a free trigger or the start already gave the player that type in this step, as a rumor or in the sighting message;
+   - otherwise `rumor` or `sighting` for the first request, and `covered` for the rest;
+   - when nothing is delivered for that (player, type), every request gets the same `capped` or `none`.
+
+A type goes out with its free trigger's reason if it has one, otherwise `targeted`. So a player who loses two types on one tick, or at a boundary with a type already pending, or loses one while buying another, learns about all of them in one message, and a purchase is never charged for what the step gives for free. Skipped ticks change nothing: two losses seen in one batched view make one message. Two players' requests never affect each other.
+
+**Targeted requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`, and each gets exactly one outcome, whatever the order of the batch:
+
+- `rumor` or `sighting`: something was delivered. Charge the 25 gold only for these two.
+- `covered`: this step already gives the player that type, for free or to a request of the same type lower by id. Not charged.
+- `capped`: the player already got a sighting in this snapshot (before this step).
+- `none`: nothing to sell. The player holds the type, or the player is unknown, or it is before control start, or no untracked target exists.
+- `duplicate`: the request id was seen before, or is listed twice in one batch (only its lowest (player, type) is taken). The step answers it without changing the state or drawing from the generator.
+
+`targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, view, playerId, type)` gives the same answer without drawing, so the UI can show whether buying would yield anything. A later step can differ only if it crosses a snapshot boundary first, or answer `covered` when a free trigger of that player and type in the same step gives the type anyway.
+
+## Reveals (§2, §5)
+
+All reveals fire when their tick is crossed since the last processed tick, so a skipped tick never loses one. Nothing is sent before control start.
+
+- **First full set:** the first player to hold every type of the preset triggers `final-sector` (the final island's sector) to everyone. Each holder of a full set gets `final-route` with the exact point: the first completer, later completers, and anyone who restores a broken set (with `restored: true`). A player who loses a type gets `final-route-inactive`.
+- **Minute 20:** `sector-reveal` to everyone, listing the sectors with sealed sources and the sectors with caches.
+- **Minute 28, then every 30 s:** `carrier-report` to everyone, listing the (sector, type) pairs of the newest snapshot. Skipping several beats sends one report.
+- **Minute 35** belongs to the claim code.
+
+## Messages and hidden information (§16)
+
+`stepIntel(config, state, view, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }` never writes into its input. Each message is `{ to, body }`, where `to` is `{ kind: "player", playerId }`, `{ kind: "players", playerIds }` or `{ kind: "everyone" }`. Broadcasts are `final-sector`, `sector-reveal` and `carrier-report`; every other kind goes to one player.
+
+Bodies carry sectors, island indexes and names, types, ticks and journal entry numbers. They never carry a player id, a rubbing id, or a source's, cache's or ship's position. The one exact position ever sent is the final island's, in a `final-route` to a full-set holder. The property tests check every message of every run against these rules:
+
+- six seeded runs with compressed reveal times;
+- one slice run with the real constants for 36,660 ticks;
+- one alpha run with the real constants that skips ticks.
+
+The same runs also check, after every step, that each player got at most one sighting message in it, that every free trigger needing a sighting (a loss, or a stale rumor's replacement) is either in that step's message or in the pending set, and that it waits only if the player's sighting was already spent in this snapshot or the older snapshot shows no other carrier of it. They also check that each player has at most one pending sighting message and that every deferred type goes out at the first boundary after it was capped (or is dropped only when the checker finds it ineligible, or kept only when the previous snapshot shows no other carrier of it). Every rumor is checked against the preference: a cache lead only when no sealed source of the type is left outside the player's journal, a carrier sighting only when no source or cache of the type exists. Every sighting's reason is checked to be `fresh`, `targeted` or `replacement`. Per step and (player, type), at most one request is charged, only for a lead of that type sent with the reason `targeted`, and a `covered` request always has a lead of its type in that step. A black-box check replays the compressed runs, with extra purchases added, against the same script with each step's requests and view arrays shuffled, and compares the messages, the outcomes sorted by request id and `hashState`. Their `EXERCISED` check asserts that every message kind, outcome and lead path occurred, including a deferred delivery, a free trigger sighted in its own step and a message with several types.
+
+## Building the world view from the ledger
+
+On each processed tick, the caller passes `{ tick, players, rubbings }`:
+
+- **`players`:** each player still in the match (`status` not `left`), with the ship's position in sub-units.
+- **`rubbings`:** each ledger rubbing with its `type` and its `location` resolved to a place:
+  - `source` becomes `{ kind: "source", island, x, y }` from its `LedgerSource`;
+  - `cache` becomes `{ kind: "cache", x, y }` from its `LedgerCache`;
+  - `player` becomes `{ kind: "carried", playerId }`;
+  - `duel` becomes `{ kind: "duel", playerId }`.
+
+Held types and claimed-out islands (islands with no sealed source left) follow from the rubbings, so they can't disagree with them. The ledger's sticky `freshRumors` flag isn't read. The config comes from `createIntelConfig({ preset, finalIsland, controlStartTick, map })`. The state comes from `createIntelState(config, seed)`, which starts before control start.
+
+## Decisions taken here
+
+- Held types and claimed-out islands are derived from the view's rubbings rather than passed separately.
+- A pending sighting is one message per player holding a set of types, so two types that need a sighting at once are delivered together at the next boundary, not one interval apart, and the cap stays one sighting message per 30 s before minute 28.
+- Every trigger of a step joins the step's set of (player, type) entries, with one sighting decision per player, so "learns about both at once" holds on every path: several losses, a loss with a replacement or a purchase, a batched view, and the boundary tick.
+- A start points only at sources and caches. Sightings come only from a loss, a targeted rumor or a journal replacement.
+- A free trigger that finds every copy carried but no snapshot entry to read yet waits like a capped one.
+- A targeted request whose type a free trigger (or the start) of the same step gives the player is `covered` and not charged; the type goes out with the free reason. Of two requests for one (player, type) in one step, the first by id is charged and the other `covered`. Before, both were charged.
+- Leads are decided in three phases (gather by (player, type), decide with keyed draws, answer grouped by (player, type)), so order independence holds by construction, and one player's purchase never changes another's result or draw.
+- The state's `rng` is the seed of the keyed draws and no longer advances.

+import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

+  CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS,
+  CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE,
+  CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS,
+  intelRules,
+  SECTOR_COLUMNS,

+  SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE,
+  SECTOR_ROWS,
+  TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD,
+  validateIntelRules,
+} from "./index.js";

+function issuesOf(candidate: unknown): string[] {
+  const result = validateIntelRules(candidate);
+  return result.ok ? [] : result.issues;
+}
+

+    expect(SECTOR_NAMES).toHaveLength(9);
+    expect(new Set(SECTOR_NAMES).size).toBe(9);
+    expect([CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS, CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS, SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE, CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE]).toEqual([30, 30, 20, 28]);
+    expect(TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD).toBe(25);
+    expect(intelRules).toMatchObject({
+      sightingDelayTicks: 600,
+      carrierIntervalTicks: 600,
+      sectorRevealTicks: 24_000,
+      carrierRevealTicks: 33_600,
+      targetedRumorGold: 25,
+    });
+    expect(validateIntelRules(intelRules)).toEqual({ ok: true, value: intelRules });
+  });
+
+  it("refuse a carrier interval of 0 and reveal times out of order", () => {
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, carrierIntervalTicks: 0, sightingDelayTicks: 0 }).some((issue) => issue.startsWith("carrierIntervalTicks:"))).toBe(true);
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, sectorRevealTicks: 33_600 })).toEqual([
+      "carrierRevealTicks: the carrier reveal (33600 ticks) must come after the sector reveal (33600 ticks)",
+    ]);
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, sectorRevealTicks: 40_000 })).toHaveLength(1);
+  });
+
+  it("refuse a carrier reveal that is not a multiple of the carrier interval", () => {
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, carrierRevealTicks: 33_601 })).toEqual([
+      "carrierRevealTicks: the carrier reveal (33601 ticks) must be a multiple of the carrier interval (600 ticks)",
+    ]);
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, carrierIntervalTicks: 100, sightingDelayTicks: 100, sectorRevealTicks: 1_000, carrierRevealTicks: 2_050 })).toHaveLength(1);
+    expect(validateIntelRules({ ...intelRules, carrierIntervalTicks: 100, sightingDelayTicks: 100, sectorRevealTicks: 1_000, carrierRevealTicks: 2_000 }).ok).toBe(true);
+    expect(intelRules.carrierRevealTicks % intelRules.carrierIntervalTicks).toBe(0);
+  });
+
+  it("refuse a delay that differs from the interval, bad names, fractional or missing values and unknown fields", () => {

+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, sectorNames: [...SECTOR_NAMES.slice(0, 8), SECTOR_NAMES[0]] })).toEqual(["sectorNames: sector names must be unique"]);
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, sectorNames: [...SECTOR_NAMES.slice(0, 8), ""] })[0]).toMatch(/^sectorNames\.8:/);
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, sectorColumns: 0 })[0]).toMatch(/^sectorColumns:/);

+    const { carrierRevealTicks: _, ...missing } = intelRules;
+    expect(issuesOf(missing)[0]).toMatch(/^carrierRevealTicks:/);
+    expect(issuesOf({ ...intelRules, extra: 1 })).toHaveLength(1);
+  });
+});

+import { z } from "zod";
+import { formatIssues, type ValidationResult } from "../rules.js";
+import { WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND } from "../sailing.js";
+
+/** The sea is split into a grid of named sectors this many columns wide and rows high (§2's "sectors"). */
+export const SECTOR_COLUMNS = 3;
+export const SECTOR_ROWS = 3;
+
+/** The nine sector names, row by row from the north-west corner. */
+export const SECTOR_NAMES = [
+  "North-West Reach",
+  "Northern Waters",
+  "North-East Reach",
+  "Western Waters",
+  "Central Waters",
+  "Eastern Waters",
+  "South-West Reach",
+  "Southern Waters",
+  "South-East Reach",
+] as const;
+
+/**
+ * §11: a carrier sighting is coarse and delayed. It reads the carrier snapshot taken one interval before the latest,
+ * so it is at least this old (and less than twice this old), never the current location.
+ */
+export const CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS = 30;
+/** §2: from minute 28 the carriers' sectors are published every 30 seconds; the carrier snapshots keep the same beat. */
+export const CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 30;
+/** §2: at minute 20 the sectors holding unclaimed rubbings and abandoned caches are revealed. */
+export const SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE = 20;
+/** §2: from minute 28 the carriers' approximate sectors are published. */
+export const CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE = 28;
+/** §11: what the caller charges for a targeted rumor that delivers something. */
+export const TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD = 25;
+
+/** The information rules (§2, §3, §11) in world ticks (20 a second), counted from the start of player control. */
+export const intelRulesSchema = z
+  .strictObject({
+    sectorColumns: z.int().positive(),
+    sectorRows: z.int().positive(),
+    /** Row by row from the north-west; one unique, non-empty name per sector. */
+    sectorNames: z.array(z.string().min(1)),
+    /** How old a carrier sighting is at least; it must equal the carrier interval, since sightings read the previous snapshot. */
+    sightingDelayTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    /** The beat of the carrier snapshots, of the sighting cap and, from the carrier reveal on, of the carrier broadcasts. */
+    carrierIntervalTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    /** Ticks from control start to the reveal of the sectors holding unclaimed rubbings and caches. */
+    sectorRevealTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    /** Ticks from control start to the first carrier broadcast: a multiple of the carrier interval, so it falls on a snapshot boundary. */
+    carrierRevealTicks: z.int().positive(),
+    targetedRumorGold: z.int().nonnegative(),
+  })
+  .superRefine((rules, ctx) => {
+    if (rules.sectorNames.length !== rules.sectorColumns * rules.sectorRows) {
+      ctx.addIssue({
+        code: "custom",
+        path: ["sectorNames"],
+        message: `${rules.sectorNames.length} names for a ${rules.sectorColumns} × ${rules.sectorRows} grid`,
+      });
+    }
+    if (new Set(rules.sectorNames).size !== rules.sectorNames.length) {
+      ctx.addIssue({ code: "custom", path: ["sectorNames"], message: "sector names must be unique" });
+    }
+    if (rules.sightingDelayTicks !== rules.carrierIntervalTicks) {
+      ctx.addIssue({
+        code: "custom",
+        path: ["sightingDelayTicks"],
+        message: `the sighting delay (${rules.sightingDelayTicks} ticks) must equal the carrier interval (${rules.carrierIntervalTicks} ticks)`,
+      });
+    }
+    if (rules.sectorRevealTicks >= rules.carrierRevealTicks) {
+      ctx.addIssue({
+        code: "custom",
+        path: ["carrierRevealTicks"],
+        message: `the carrier reveal (${rules.carrierRevealTicks} ticks) must come after the sector reveal (${rules.sectorRevealTicks} ticks)`,
+      });
+    }
+    // The broadcasts must fall on snapshot boundaries, so a pending sighting and a new one never split across messages.
+    if (rules.carrierIntervalTicks > 0 && rules.carrierRevealTicks % rules.carrierIntervalTicks !== 0) {
+      ctx.addIssue({
+        code: "custom",
+        path: ["carrierRevealTicks"],
+        message: `the carrier reveal (${rules.carrierRevealTicks} ticks) must be a multiple of the carrier interval (${rules.carrierIntervalTicks} ticks)`,
+      });
+    }
+  });
+
+export type IntelRules = z.infer<typeof intelRulesSchema>;
+
+export const intelRules: IntelRules = {
+  sectorColumns: SECTOR_COLUMNS,
+  sectorRows: SECTOR_ROWS,
+  sectorNames: [...SECTOR_NAMES],
+  sightingDelayTicks: CARRIER_SIGHTING_DELAY_SECONDS * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  carrierIntervalTicks: CARRIER_INTERVAL_SECONDS * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  sectorRevealTicks: SECTOR_REVEAL_MINUTE * 60 * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  carrierRevealTicks: CARRIER_REVEAL_MINUTE * 60 * WORLD_STEPS_PER_SECOND,
+  targetedRumorGold: TARGETED_RUMOR_GOLD,
+};
+
+export function validateIntelRules(candidate: unknown): ValidationResult<IntelRules> {

+
+/** Recursively frozen, so a step that mutated its input would throw. */
+function deepFreeze<T>(value: T): T {
+  if (typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Object.isFrozen(value)) {
+    Object.freeze(value);
+    for (const child of Object.values(value)) deepFreeze(child);
+  }
+  return value;

+
+function viewOf(tick: number, world: World): IntelWorldView {
+  return { tick, players: Object.entries(world.players).map(([id, at]) => ({ id, ...at })), rubbings: world.rubbings };

+/** Steps with frozen input and state, checking neither changes. */
+class Run {
+  state: IntelState;
+  constructor(

+  step(tick: number, world: World, requests: TargetedRumorRequest[] = []): IntelStepResult {
+    const view = deepFreeze(viewOf(tick, world));
+    const before = hashState(deepFreeze(this.state));
+    const stepped = stepIntel(this.config, this.state, view, deepFreeze(requests));
+    expect(hashState(this.state)).toBe(before);
+    this.state = stepped.state;
+    return stepped;
+  }
+
+  available(tick: number, world: World, playerId: string, type: RubbingType) {
+    return targetedRumorAvailability(this.config, this.state, viewOf(tick, world), playerId, type);
+  }

+    ]);

1	# Task: intel
2	
3	## Goal
4	
5	Build the match's information systems as pure, deterministic rules. They tell a player where to go and when the race tightens:
6	- rumors that point toward a missing rubbing type;
7	- the journal that marks stale leads and offers replacements;
8	- coarse, delayed carrier sightings;
9	- the sea sectors;
10	- the timed reveals of §2 (the final-island sector when a first full set exists, minute-20 reveals, minute-28 carrier sectors every 30 s).
11	
12	This information is what turns exploring into a race and brings players into conflict, so it must be useful but never a free tracker. Every output is addressed to specific players (§16). `objectives-endgame` wires it into the match room later. This feature only builds and proves the rules.
13	
14	## Context
15	
16	- Read `docs/spec.md` §2 (the phase table and "Time limits and results"), §3 ("Exploration activities": rumors, stale rumors, journal), §5 (first full set: the final route to the eligible player, the broad sector to everyone), §11 ("Preventing runaway leaders": a free fresh rumor on loss, the coarse delayed carrier sighting; the targeted rumor costs 25 gold) and §16 (hidden information).
17	- Read `docs/architecture.md` and the pure modules this one sits beside and must match in style: `packages/simulation/src/objectives` (the ledger: rubbing locations, `freshRumors`) and `packages/simulation/src/claim` (the step shape and seeded property tests), plus `packages/content/src/seaMap.ts` (map size, islands) and `tests/unit/purity.test.ts`.
18	- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
19	- Other features run at the same time and own the sea, server, web, tests, the duel and `packages/*/src/ruins`. Stay inside your owned paths.
20	- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**
21	
22	## Constraints
23	
24	- Owned paths only: `packages/simulation/src/intel`, `packages/content/src/intel`, `docs/intel.md`, and `packages/simulation/package.json` and `packages/content/package.json` **only to add one subpath export each** (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel`, following the existing pattern with the `@pirate-sea-race/source` condition first). Do not change their `postbuild` scripts, dependencies, any existing source file, barrel, tsconfig or root file.
25	- Independent of the ledger's code: the caller passes a per-tick **world view** (for each rubbing, its type and where it is: a sealed source with its island, a cache position, a carrier with position, or reserved in a duel; each player's held types and position; which islands are claimed out). Don't import `objectives`, so the two stay decoupled. Gold for bought rumors is the caller's (ledger) business; this module only generates the rumor.
26	- Pure and integer: no Phaser, Colyseus, DOM, timers, wall-clock time, `Math.random` or floating-point transcendental functions. Time is the world tick (20 per second). Randomness comes from the seeded generator (`random.ts`). Durations are named content constants in seconds, converted to ticks.
27	- The step shape: `stepIntel(config, state, worldView, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }`. Every message names its recipients: one player, several, or everyone. It never mutates its input.
28	- **Targeted rumor requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`. Each gets exactly one outcome, `{ requestId, result: "rumor" | "sighting" | "capped" | "none" | "duplicate" }`, so the caller charges 25 gold only for `rumor` or `sighting`. A repeated `requestId` is answered `duplicate` without changing the state or using the generator. An exported pure `targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, worldView, playerId, type)` lets the UI show whether buying would yield anything.
29	
30	## Design (settled)
31	
32	- **Sectors.** The map is divided into a 3 × 3 grid of named sectors (for example "North-West Reach", "Central Waters"), computed from the map size in the config. `sectorOf(position)` is total and deterministic on the boundaries.
33	- **Rumors.** A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island** (a sealed source of that type there) or a **sector** (a cache or a carrier). It never names a rubbing id or an exact position. Generation picks, deterministically from the seed, among the eligible targets for a type the player lacks. It prefers sealed sources, then caches, then a carrier sighting. It never picks a target that is the player's own inventory. Rumors are made in four cases:
34	  - a **starting rumor** for each player at control start (§2);
35	  - a **fresh rumor** when the world view shows a type was stolen from the player (§11);

# Task: intel

## Goal

Build the match's information systems as pure, deterministic rules. They tell a player where to go and when the race tightens:
- rumors that point toward a missing rubbing type;
- the journal that marks stale leads and offers replacements;
- coarse, delayed carrier sightings;
- the sea sectors;
- the timed reveals of §2 (the final-island sector when a first full set exists, minute-20 reveals, minute-28 carrier sectors every 30 s).

This information is what turns exploring into a race and brings players into conflict, so it must be useful but never a free tracker. Every output is addressed to specific players (§16). `objectives-endgame` wires it into the match room later. This feature only builds and proves the rules.

## Context

- Read `docs/spec.md` §2 (the phase table and "Time limits and results"), §3 ("Exploration activities": rumors, stale rumors, journal), §5 (first full set: the final route to the eligible player, the broad sector to everyone), §11 ("Preventing runaway leaders": a free fresh rumor on loss, the coarse delayed carrier sighting; the targeted rumor costs 25 gold) and §16 (hidden information).
- Read `docs/architecture.md` and the pure modules this one sits beside and must match in style: `packages/simulation/src/objectives` (the ledger: rubbing locations, `freshRumors`) and `packages/simulation/src/claim` (the step shape and seeded property tests), plus `packages/content/src/seaMap.ts` (map size, islands) and `tests/unit/purity.test.ts`.
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Other features run at the same time and own the sea, server, web, tests, the duel and `packages/*/src/ruins`. Stay inside your owned paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Constraints

- Owned paths only: `packages/simulation/src/intel`, `packages/content/src/intel`, `docs/intel.md`, and `packages/simulation/package.json` and `packages/content/package.json` **only to add one subpath export each** (`@pirate-sea-race/simulation/intel`, `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel`, following the existing pattern with the `@pirate-sea-race/source` condition first). Do not change their `postbuild` scripts, dependencies, any existing source file, barrel, tsconfig or root file.
- Independent of the ledger's code: the caller passes a per-tick **world view** (for each rubbing, its type and where it is: a sealed source with its island, a cache position, a carrier with position, or reserved in a duel; each player's held types and position; which islands are claimed out). Don't import `objectives`, so the two stay decoupled. Gold for bought rumors is the caller's (ledger) business; this module only generates the rumor.
- Pure and integer: no Phaser, Colyseus, DOM, timers, wall-clock time, `Math.random` or floating-point transcendental functions. Time is the world tick (20 per second). Randomness comes from the seeded generator (`random.ts`). Durations are named content constants in seconds, converted to ticks.
- The step shape: `stepIntel(config, state, worldView, requests) → { state, messages, outcomes }`. Every message names its recipients: one player, several, or everyone. It never mutates its input.
- **Targeted rumor requests** are `{ requestId, playerId, type }`. Each gets exactly one outcome, `{ requestId, result: "rumor" | "sighting" | "capped" | "none" | "duplicate" }`, so the caller charges 25 gold only for `rumor` or `sighting`. A repeated `requestId` is answered `duplicate` without changing the state or using the generator. An exported pure `targetedRumorAvailability(config, state, worldView, playerId, type)` lets the UI show whether buying would yield anything.

## Design (settled)

- **Sectors.** The map is divided into a 3 × 3 grid of named sectors (for example "North-West Reach", "Central Waters"), computed from the map size in the config. `sectorOf(position)` is total and deterministic on the boundaries.
- **Rumors.** A rumor names a missing type and a target: an **island** (a sealed source of that type there) or a **sector** (a cache or a carrier). It never names a rubbing id or an exact position. Generation picks, deterministically from the seed, among the eligible targets for a type the player lacks. It prefers sealed sources, then caches, then a carrier sighting. It never picks a target that is the player's own inventory. Rumors are made in four cases:
  - a **starting rumor** for each player at control start (§2);
  - a **fresh rumor** when the world view shows a type was stolen from the player (§11);
  - a **targeted rumor** on request, gold-gated by the caller (§11);
  - a **replacement lead** from the journal.
- **Two kinds of lead.**
  - **Journal rumors** target only islands (sealed sources) or cache sectors. Only these go stale: when the target no longer holds a copy of that type, the rumor is marked stale (a message to its holder, with the tick), and the journal offers a replacement from the remaining sources and caches.
  - A **carrier sighting** is a one-shot message: the sector where a carrier of that type was 30 s earlier, never the current one. It is **never** tracked for staleness, so carrier movement can't leak live information. It is sent only on three triggers: a fresh rumor after a loss when every other copy is carried, a targeted rumor under the same condition, or a journal replacement when every remaining copy is carried. At most one carrier sighting per player per carrier interval (30 s) before minute 28.
  - A rumor whose type its holder has since obtained is retired quietly (a "resolved" message, no replacement).
- **Carrier snapshots (not a rolling history).** At each 30 s carrier boundary counted from control start (crossing-based), the state takes one snapshot: the sector, type and internal holder of each carried copy. It keeps only the latest two. A carrier sighting reads the **older** snapshot, so it is 30–60 s old and never the current location, by construction. The minute-28 broadcast reads the newer one. Snapshot entries held by the requester themselves are never used for that requester's sighting.
- **The sighting cap** lines up with the snapshots: at most one sighting per player per snapshot, before minute 28. A **free** trigger (a fresh rumor after a loss, or a journal replacement) that hits the cap is **deferred**, not dropped: it is delivered at the next snapshot boundary (at most one pending per player).
- **Held types include rubbings reserved in a duel**, as the ledger's `heldTypes` counts them. So entering a duel is never a "loss", and only a settled theft is.
- **What sightings and broadcasts contain:** a sector and a rubbing type, never a player id, a rubbing id or an exact position.
- **Losses and completions come from diffing** each player's held types between ticks. The ledger's sticky `freshRumors` flag isn't used as a signal.
- **Robust to skipped ticks:** reveals and intervals fire when a boundary is crossed since the last processed tick (`>=`), not on equality, so a skipped or batched tick never loses one.
- **Timed reveals** (§2), counted from control start (`controlStartTick` in the config):
  - **The first full set:** when a player first holds all the preset's types, everyone gets the final island's sector, and that player gets the exact final-island position (their "route"). If they lose a type, their route becomes inactive until the set is restored. A later completer gets their own route message. The final island's position comes from the config.
  - **Minute 20:** everyone gets the sectors that contain unclaimed rubbings (sealed sources) and abandoned caches.
  - **Minute 28 on:** every 30 s, everyone gets the approximate sectors of rubbing carriers.
  - **Minute 35:** nothing here; the claim code ends the match.
- **Hidden information.** No message to a player contains another player's exact position, a rubbing id or a source's exact location. The only exact position ever sent is the final island's, and only to a complete-set player. A test asserts this over every message of every property run.

## Acceptance

Each item names the test that proves it. Tests live in `packages/simulation/src/intel` unless noted.

1. **Sectors:** every map cell maps to exactly one of nine sectors; the boundaries are deterministic; the names are unique.
2. **Rumors:** scripted tests for each of the four cases:
   - targets prefer sources, then caches, then carriers;
   - there is never a rumor for a type the player holds, and never one pointing at the player's own inventory;
   - the same seed gives the same rumor.
3. **Staleness and the journal:** scripted tests:
   - an island or cache target emptied by collection (a source collected, a cache claimed) goes stale, and the journal offers a replacement from the remaining sources and caches;
   - a rumor whose type the holder then obtains (by collection or theft) is resolved, not stale;
   - with every copy carried, the replacement is a carrier sighting from the older snapshot (30–60 s old, never current);
   - a capped free trigger is delivered at the next boundary;
   - the targeted-request outcomes cover all five results, including `duplicate` with the very same state.
4. **Reveals:** scripted tests at the exact boundary ticks:
   - the first full set, including a lost-then-restored set and a second completer;
   - minute 20;
   - minute 28, then every 30 s;
   - nothing before control start.
5. **Hidden information:** seeded property runs (random worlds with players collecting, stealing, caching and moving) check every message against the rules in the design:
   - at least one seed runs the real constants for 36,000+ ticks, past minute 28 plus several carrier intervals; the other seeds use a config with compressed reveal times;
   - no message has an id or an exact position (except the final island to a full-set holder);
   - no player gets more than one carrier sighting per snapshot before minute 28;
   - no stale message is ever sent for a carrier sighting;
   - some runs skip ticks. The state replays to the same `hashState`. An `EXERCISED` coverage check asserts that every message kind occurred.
6. **Content:** the constants (the sector grid 3 × 3, the sighting delay 30 s, the reveal times 20 min and 28 min, the carrier interval 30 s, the sector names) live in `@pirate-sea-race/content/intel` with a zod validator. A content test refuses a carrier interval of 0 and reveal times out of order.
7. **Docs:** `docs/intel.md`, about a page: sectors, rumor generation and staleness, the reveal schedule, the message addressing, and how the caller builds the world view from the ledger.
8. `npm ci` then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build` pass from a clean checkout, and the purity test covers the new directories.

## Stop

Report `blocked` instead of continuing when any of these happens:

# Task: intel

## Goal

Deliver `intel-core` (the pure rumors, journal, sectors and reveals) with its remaining review findings fixed. Run intel-core-fixes-001 fixed the first deferred-sighting bug and passed every check, but its general reviewer found the same symptom on another path. Sightings triggered on one tick are still handled one type at a time, so the second type waits up to a whole interval. Start from that run's snapshot, fix it for good, and the whole feature is reviewed again.

## Context

- `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` and `decisions.md`, and `features/intel-core-fixes/intel-task.md` and `decisions.md`, define the feature, and all of it still applies. Read them first.
- **First step:** restore intel-core-fixes-001's snapshot (commit `2309421`) into your worktree, deletions included, but not `features/`:
  `git restore --source=refs/workflow/57859d023c4770f7/intel --staged --worktree -- . ':!features'`.
  Check with `git diff --stat refs/workflow/57859d023c4770f7/intel -- . ':!features'` (it must print nothing). Then read `docs/intel.md` and `packages/simulation/src/intel/step.ts` (`freeLead`, `flushPending`, lines 380–440).
- The verifier runs `npm ci`, then `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test:unit`, `npm run test:integration` and `npm run build`.
- Other features run at the same time and own other paths. Stay inside your owned paths.
- **This machine is shared by several runs. Never stop processes by name pattern (`pkill -f`, `killall`, and so on). Stop only the PIDs you started.**

## Findings to fix (general reviewer)

1. **(P1) One sighting decision per player per step.** Today `freeLead` runs once per type (`step.ts:417` for losses, `:434` for replacements), and the first uncapped call flushes a one-type message and uses up the snapshot's sighting.
   - **Fix: one accumulator, one emit point.** Each player gets one sighting accumulator per step, a sorted set of types.
     - It starts with the player's pending set if a boundary was crossed.
     - Losses, journal replacements **and targeted requests** all add their type to it. None of them flushes on its own.
     - After every pass of the step, each player gets exactly one decision. If the cap allows (or it's minute 28 or later), emit **one** message listing every still-eligible type from the older snapshot, and answer each targeted request in it `sighting`. Otherwise keep the **free** types as the single pending set, and answer targeted requests `capped`. A capped paid type is never queued, so a purchase is never charged for something deferred.
     - The message's type order and sector choice must not depend on the order in which triggers were added.
   - **Scripted tests:**
     - two uncapped losses on one tick give one message with both types;
     - a loss plus a replacement on one tick give one message;
     - a loss plus a targeted request on one tick give one message, and the request is `sighting`;
     - a capped tick with a loss and a targeted request leaves the loss pending and the request `capped`;
     - two losses in one batched view (skipped ticks) give one message;
     - a trigger on the boundary tick itself is included in that boundary's message.
   - **Property checker:** at most one sighting message per player per step. Every free trigger is delivered in that step's message or the next boundary's. Fix `docs/intel.md` wherever it describes this.
2. **(P2) No carrier sighting on the start trigger.** A starting rumor (§2) targets only sealed sources or caches. If every copy of a missing type is carried at the start (for example a late joiner), the starting rumor goes to another missing type that has a source or cache target (§2's "a rumor leading toward a reachable objective"). Only when no missing type has one is there no starting rumor (documented). A start never produces a carrier sighting, as `features/intel-core/intel-task.md` specifies (sightings only on a fresh loss, a targeted rumor, or a journal replacement). Update the scripted test that asserts the old behaviour, and add `start`'s carried-only case to the tests. `EXERCISED` stays with the three sighting triggers.
